subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a Slack-plugin search action, and what action-token, user-token, retention, redaction, scope, and read-target boundary should it use?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but it authorizes workspace search through Slack tokens and cannot be safely delegated to automation until maintainers choose the token and privacy contract.

options.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` in the Slack plugin with thread/user/account-bound action-token handling, no generic token exposure, least-privilege scopes, tests, docs, and live proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search direction
options.body: Define one Slack search contract that covers both RTS and user-token search before any implementation lands.

options.title: Defer Slack workspace search
options.body: Keep the issue open but block implementation until maintainers are ready to own the workspace-search security model.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` in the Slack plugin with thread/user/account-bound action-token handling, no generic token exposure, least-privilege scopes, tests, docs, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He recently routed the broad Slack search/action bundle back to this issue and has adjacent Slack feature/config history.
